([[Chandler, Arizona]]) | college = [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] (2021–2024) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2024 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2024]]) * [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 co-Player of the Year]] (2024) * 2× First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2023, 2024) * Second-team All-Atlantic 10 (2022) * Atlantic 10 Defensive Player of the Year (2024) * Atlantic 10 Rookie of the Year (2022) }} '''DaRon Holmes II''' (born August 15, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Holmes grew up in [[Goodyear, Arizona]] and initially attended [[Millennium High School (Arizona)|Millennium High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-flyers-fab-freshman-daron-holmes-ii-its-all-about-where-you-fit/4UFXKVIQD5DVNJGHZXBTT7QMHA/|title=Archdeacon: Flyers' fab freshman DaRon Holmes II|first=Tom|last=Archdeacon|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=December 12, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2022}} He was named the Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 23.7 points, 10.6 rebounds, 3.8 blocks, and 3.1 assists per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/ua-target-daron-holmes-named-arizona-gatorade-player-of-the-year/article_44ddb7f4-6fd0-11ea-94c2-bbd51c6c84b7.html|title= UA target DaRon Holmes named Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year|first=Justin|last=Spears|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=March 28, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]] prior to the start of his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/10/24/two-time-all-arizona-basketball-player-daron-holmes-commits-dayton/6023155002/|title=Two-time All-Arizona basketball player DaRon Holmes commits to Dayton|first=Richard|last=Obert|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=October 24, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2022}} He ultimately moved back to Arizona during his winter break and transferred a second time to AZ Compass Prep School in [[Chandler, Arizona]].{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/01/05/daron-holmes-transfers-montverde-academy-az-compass-prep/6557551002/|title=DaRon Holmes transfers from Montverde Academy to AZ Compass Prep|first=Richard|last=Obert|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=January 5, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], and [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]].{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-flyers-land-top-40-recruit-in-class-of-2021/F5B6GA2RKZGOZOMICAB6VMDDG4/|title=Dayton Flyers land top-40 recruit in class of 2021|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=October 24, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2022}} ==College career== Holmes started all 35 of the Dayton Flyers' games as a freshman and led the team with 12.8 points per game and also averaged 6.1 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/holmes-on-second-season-at-dayton-i-just-want-to-win/3WFWD6BY5ZB5VONFDWSOY6UTFQ/|title=Dayton Flyers forward DaRon Holmes adds weight to take his game to the next level|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=July 15, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022}} He also set a school record with 81 total blocks in a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/01/31/daron-holmes-breaks-dayton-blocked-shots-record/9288931002/|title=DaRon Holmes breaks Dayton blocked shots record|first=Richard|last=Obert|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes was named the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] Rookie of the Year, second-team All-Atlantic 10, and to the conference All-Defense team.{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/3653195/2022/10/21/dayton-basketball-anthony-grant-daron-holmes/|title=How Dayton, led by Anthony Grant and DaRon Holmes, are building on success|first=Brian|last=Hamilton|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 21, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes entered his sophomore season on the watch list for the [[Karl Malone Award]].{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/daytons-holmes-named-to-watch-list-for-national-award/VHI4T5AISJHSFAE23ASJC7IFXQ/|title=Dayton’s Holmes named to watch list for national award|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=October 27, 2022|access-date=October 28, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18.4 points, 8.1 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game and was named first-team All-Atlantic 10 team. On April 24, 2023, Holmes declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2023/04/nba-draft-daron-holmes-early-entry-testing-waters-dayton|title=Dayton center DaRon Holmes quietly declared for NBA draft while maintaining NCAA eligibility|first=Bryan|last=Kalbrosky|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 24, 2023|access-date=November 27, 2023}} He later withdrew from the draft on the day of the deadline and announced that he would return to Dayton for his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/holmes-will-return-to-dayton-after-withdrawing-from-draft/C4BP7NPMPVGAFO7QLOEPKKMRO4/|title=Holmes will return to Dayton after withdrawing from NBA Draft|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=May 31, 2023|access-date=November 27, 2023}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics
